id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point per chip-select: one xSPI/QSPI/OSPI controller (master) drives SCLK + CS# and the bidirectional data lines IO0..IO7 to one memory device per CS#. Unlike I2C/SMBus this is NOT a shared multi-drop addressed bus; each device has its own chip-select.

supported_topologies.name: Single controller, multiple devices
supported_topologies.description: One controller with multiple CS# lines, one per device.

supported_topologies.name: Quad / Octal width
supported_topologies.description: 4 or 8 shared bidirectional data lines per device.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Drives SCLK, CS#, the instruction/address/dummy phases, and the data lines when writing.
Responds to its CS#; drives the data lines (and DQS) during reads, latches data during writes.

bidirectional_mode.description: When SPC0=1, single data pin is used; MOSI becomes MOMI (master) or MISO becomes SISO (slave). BIDIROE controls the direction of the chosen pin.

fields.interconnect_role: QSPI/OSPI is a controller-to-memory expansion of SPI. The controller selects a device with CS#, issues the phase protocol, and reads or writes the device's linear flash address space; it may expose a memory-mapped XIP window to the SoC.

ordering_guarantees.point_to_point: Each device addressed by a dedicated chip-select, not by an on-bus device address.

ss_handling_per_topology.point_to_point_CPHA0: SS must toggle HIGH between bytes (min tI high time).
ss_handling_per_topology.point_to_point_CPHA1: SS may stay LOW continuously for back-to-back transfers.
ss_handling_per_topology.multi_slave: Each slave's SS individually driven LOW only when addressed.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: QSPI/OSPI accesses a linear byte-addressed flash memory space (3- or 4-byte address). The opcode space (0x00..0xFF) selects read/program/erase/status/config functions; xSPI adds a configuration-register interface.

slave_classification.duplex_slave: Capable of both transmit and receive; standard SPI slave.
slave_classification.receive_only_slave: Simpler slaves with no MISO output drive; master will not receive data from them.

default_signal_values_evidence_tables: Table 4-1 Normal Mode and Bidirectional Mode
